notes.title: Quality of Life Patch - Patch Notes 11.4.2024
notes.content:
Hello everybody! Thank you all for playing and enjoying Fear the Spotlight.
We're happy to share our patch based on all the feedback and bug reports we've been getting. Thank you for your help, and sorry for any inconvenience these issues may have caused.

[b]Patch Notes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed save files in Amy’s house breaking on some PCs
[*] Fixed shed lock puzzle getting stuck on some PCs
[*] Fixed keyboard key rebinding
[*] Improved Japanese translation.
[*] Improved framerate throughout the house.
[*] Red numbers in the lockpick minigame now pulse (for colorblind players).
[*] Updated "Special Thanks."
[*] Fixed lighting bugs in the girls' locker room and theater.
[*] Fixed several issues when fading to black between scenes.
[*] Corrected ceiling geometry in the dark library.
[*] Fixed retro (wobbly) material on various objects.
[*] Fixed hanging spotlight in house unexpectedly turning off
[*] Fixed attic enemy behavior when playing at 120fps+.
[*] Adjusted SSAO to reduce temporal artifacts.
[*] Improved edge-cases in the faculty office setup.
[*] Fixed cell phone rotation bug when toggling menus too quickly.
[*] Fixed collision on air vents.
[*] Fixed checkpoints sometimes failing in Chapter 2
[*] Fixed sliding door lock sometimes getting stuck
[*] Improved clarity for unlocking Chapter 2
[*] Added "info" screen to main menu
[/list]

notes.title: Fear the Spotlight review: Blumhouse Games’ ghost story debut is a promising start
notes.content:
Spooky season is well under way following the successful launch of the Silent Hill 2 remake, but fans of survival horror have more to look forward to this month with the release of Cozy Game Pals’ Fear the Spotlight. The first of multiple projects that Blumhouse Games has plans to publish, Fear the Spotlight is a suitably creepy, teen-slasher style romp that — while not all that scary for the most part — is a strong start for the publisher’s upcoming slate of games.

Read more

notes.title: Fear the Spotlight (PS5) Review
notes.content:
Fear the Spotlight has an interesting background. Initially released in September of last year, it was pulled from the Steam store after receiving an infusion from Blumhouse and its new video game publishing arm. The game was re-released this year, now on consoles, with the addition of the second half of the story and more development time to QA some bugs. As the first of many games to be published by Blumhouse, Fear the Spotlight has garnered significant attention to set the tone for what to expect from Blumhouse’s gaming ventures. Cozy Game Pals has put their best foot forward, and the game has certainly piqued my interest.

Fear the Spotlight follows Amy and Vivian, who venture into their school library after hours with the intention of conducting a séance. What begins as a seemingly innocent exploration of the supernatural quickly turns into a terrifying journey, filled with haunting revelations about a school fire from decades ago. Unknown to Vivian, Amy has already... Read more

notes.title: Fear the Spotlight's demo is a great way to kick off the spooky season even if it did make me face one of my irrational fears
notes.content: I'm not massively superstitious, but I was given access to far too many horror films at a young age, so I think it's understandable that I'm at least wary of the supernatural. This being said, the one thing that I've taken away from watching movies like Paranormal Activity, The Exorcist, and What Lies Beneath is that you should never, under any circumstances, mess with ouija boards. But unfortunately I had to suspend my most hard-and-fast rule when playing the PS1-style survival horror, Fear the Spotlight's demo, and I'm still angry about it... Read more.

notes.title: Retro '90s horror game Fear the Spotlight returns to Steam after a year
notes.content:
Horror has lost something in recent years, in part because the fidelity of games has massively improved. In the 1990s you would be forced to fill in what you were seeing and experiencing with your imagination, making something far scarier than anything that was actually happening on screen. The most terrifying place to be is inside your imagination which is why classics like Silent Hill and Resident Evil remain compelling, so many years later. Fear the Spotlight is a game that understands this very well, with a retro aesthetic that tugs at the darkest recesses of your brain, and it's finally about to get its full release on Steam.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: New horror game Fear the Spotlight is the '90s hit you need
notes.content:
While modern horror games are growing ever more elaborate, there's still something quite unnerving about that '90s 3D aesthetic. With classics like Silent Hill and Resident Evil using the design and tech limitations of the time to create fear-inducing yet alluring low-polygon worlds, horror fans still hold that nascent era of classic horror gaming in high regard. Putting their keen eyes on nostalgia, the developers behind the upcoming Fear the Spotlight are hoping to craft an experience that captures that same sense of low-poly dread and unease, and from what I saw at Summer Game Fest, they're doing it pretty well.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Blumhouse Games reveals its first release: A PS1-style horror adventure that promises no jump scares
notes.content: Production studio Blumhouse announced a move into videogames in 2023 with a new division called Blumhouse Games, which it said will "partner with independent game developers to bring their creative vision to life via original, horror-themed games." Today we got our look at the very first project to come out of that effort, and it certainly seems to fit that billing... Read more.

Thanks to your amazing support and reception of Fear the Spotlight's original release, we caught the attention of [url=https://blumhouse.com/games]Blumhouse Games[/url]. They loved the game so much that they offered to help us in any way they could. We’re still in disbelief!

We can't wait to share more with you soon!

notes.content:
Dear Fans!

Hi there, it's Bryan and Crista! We've got some exciting news that will have an impact on Fear the Spotlight in the near future.

First, we want to thank everyone who has played Fear the Spotlight so far. Thanks to your incredible support, we've been given the opportunity to keep working on the game to make it even better. We'll be adding console versions, improving translations, offering more languages, and (most excitingly) [b]adding some new gameplay[/b].

We want to be upfront with you – [b]We'll be taking the game off Steam[/b] while we work on these improvements. We'd love for you to wait for the improved version, but if you were looking forward to playing it this Halloween season, you will have until [b]November 2nd[/b] to purchase the game as it is now. We can't thank you enough for playing our game. It means the world to us to see how much you're enjoying it. We're super excited about what's in store and can't wait to share more details with you.

With loads of gratitude and excitement,

notes.title: Development Update: We're still Stirring in Sunnyside High
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42282789/0577cceff4cffaab73fc11648593a6345a261237.gif[/img]
Welcome back, fans of Fear the Spotlight. It's been a year since you experienced the terror of Sunnyside High, and we've been lurking in the shadows, tirelessly working on bringing you an even more terrifying experience. We can't wait to share some improvements you will see in the full game:

⦁	[b]Physical Puzzles: [/b]We've taken inspiration from escape rooms to make the puzzles and exploration more immersive.
⦁	[b]An Intelligent Presence:[/b] The enemy has become more than just a predictable obstacle. We've upgraded its mind to keep you on edge and constantly guessing.
⦁	[b]Heart-pounding moments: [/b]We've added much needed scary encounters that are not just puzzles or sneaking. These are moments that will test the limits of your courage
⦁	[b]More areas to uncover: [/b]We've opened up new areas of the school for you to explore, each with its own puzzles and stories to discover.

Stay tuned for more updates as we approach the final stages of development. The secrets of Sunnyside High are waiting to be uncovered, but are you brave enough to face them?

notes.title: Our demo is a hit! Here's what's next.
notes.content:
[h2]Demo Reaction[/h2]

We released the playable demo 2 weeks ago,  and the reaction has been way huger than we ever expected. Comments, plays, wishlists (please wishlist on Steam), and even trending as 3rd most popular game on all of Itch.io!

It's an amazing feeling to see people actually understand our inspirations and care about the mystery we are putting so much work into building.

Thank you, thank you,[b] thank you SO MUCH[/b]. You have no idea.


[h2]Your Questions Answered[/h2]

We've been getting lots of questions (mostly about about the "full game") and I want to try my best to keep you all in the loop:


[h3]Release Date[/h3]
By far the most frequent question is [b]"when is the full game coming out?" [/b]
The short answer is: not soon.
The demo is really all we have so far, the rest of the game only exists on paper. And because we didn't expect a big reaction, our paper design was very minimal (maybe 1-hour long) And would have taken a few months to make.
But the reaction HAS been big, so we've spent these 2 weeks going back to the drawing board and fleshing out the design to include a lot of things we thought we had to cut.
We're still figuring out the exact scope. We're being responsible adults about it because we don't have infinite time and money, and there's only so much we can expect to earn back. But we are really narrowing down on some possibilities.


[h3]Ports[/h3]
We're being asked if the game will be released for [b]consoles and other languages[/b].
We'd love to! But the English PC version is definitely what we'll work on first. We'll worry about other releases when we are further along.
Porting and localization is a LOT of work. Even if other people are helping us, it still takes some of our time. Since our team is only two people every little bit of time matters. 

[h3]Difficulty[/h3]
Another question we're getting: The Spotlight is too easy, will the full game be [b]more challenging[/b]?
"Challenge" is really tricky because the right balance can be different for each person.
We made the call to keep The Spotlight pretty easy in the demo so people would actually finish it. In the full game we want him to be INTENSE and we are prepared to put a lot of work into getting it right.

[h3]PS1 Look[/h3]
We're also getting questions about [b]our PS1 look.[/b] 
A full breakdown is something we'd love to do for a future update.
Our overall goal is to evoke the PS1 look without being SO strict about it. We're really picking and choosing what WE think looks good.
Some people are saying that our filters are too intense. We'll be constantly tweaking the filters until we finish, so feedback is considered. The full game will also have an accessibility option to tone things down.

[h3]Content[/h3]
And lastly we are getting lots of questions about [b]what will be in the final game[/b]. More enemies? More gear? More locations? Etcetera.
The simple answer is an excited "YES"! We have all of those things planned, but we won't know what will make it into the final game until we test and iterate and make sure it's fun.
We're really not sure how much to share about specific content because it dips into spoiler territory. A big element of horror games is the mystery and the surprise of seeing things for the first time. So it might be shame to give things away so early. That's something we'll have to figure out as we continue to update you.


[h2]Thank You[/h2]

We'll try to update you again when we have a better idea of scope and schedule. But now we really need to get back to work!

Thank you so much for following us on this journey. 

Wish us luck!
Bryan and Crista,
Cozy Game Pals
